title: The Faithful Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1917, the coastal town of Marrow's Reach is cut off when its bridge closes for repairs, trapping Vesper Dunmore, a battlefield nurse who has spent seven years recording in a hidden ledger the names of soldiers erased from official reports. Among those names is Elias Thorne, now declared an enemy combatant, to whom Vesper once promised safe passage home. As military authorities arrive to audit the hospital and hunt a suspected informant, Vesper must choose between the silence that has kept everyone alive and the promise that could destroy them. The novel ends at dawn: Vesper smuggles Elias aboard the morning ship using a dead officer's uniform and papers from the ledger itself, then surrenders the ledger to the authorities — choosing to be seen at last, whatever it costs.
about_author: Casper Galloway is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime hospital records before turning to fiction. They write about the people history files under 'miscellaneous,' and live near a tidal estuary that freezes exactly once a decade.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Vesper Dunmore, POV. On the last day before the bridge closes, Vester finishes a shift at Marrow's Reach convalescent hospital and adds three new names to the hidden ledger of soldiers omitted from official reports. The emotional beat is quiet dread: winter is coming, and so are auditors.

chapters.title: What the Bridge Carries
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The town gathers to watch the bridge close for the season; among the last to cross is Major Aldous Renwick, arriving to investigate discrepancies in casualty reports. Vesper recognizes him from France. Beat: the trap closing gently, almost politely.

chapters.title: A Promise Made in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback woven through present-tense frames, Vesper's POV. In 1914, before the war hardened, Vesper promised a young German-born orderly named Elias Thorne that if he were ever declared enemy, Vesper would get him out. Beat: tenderness shadowed by what the promise will cost.

chapters.title: The Ship on the Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper learns the supply ship Meridian will make one final sailing before the harbor ices over — and that Elias is being held at the customs house two streets away, classified as enemy alien. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Matron Ivy Calloway's POV. Matron Calloway, who suspects the ledger exists but has never looked, quietly obstructs Renwick's first interview with the staff. Beat: complicity as an act of love between people who have never spoken of it.

chapters.title: The Uniform in the Trunk
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Sorting the effects of Lieutenant Harrow, dead of fever, Vesper finds a spare officer's uniform and blank transit papers — everything needed to walk a man onto a ship, if one is willing to wear a ghost. Beat: temptation dressed in wool and brass buttons.

chapters.title: Renwick's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Major Renwick's POV. Renwick cross-references hospital ledgers against regimental returns and finds forty-one men unaccounted for. He is not cruel; he believes names must balance or the war means nothing. Beat: the antagonist revealed as a man with his own faithful ledger.

chapters.title: The Customs House Window
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper walks past the customs house each evening and once sees Elias at the barred window; they do not speak, but Elias mouths the words of their old promise. Beat: longing sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Debt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper visits the family solicitor and learns the Dunmore name — and the house — came from a grandfather whose fortune was built on shipping contraband; invisibility was always the family inheritance. Beat: identity unmoored from respectability.

chapters.title: Forty-One Names
chapters.summary: Renwick's POV. Renwick interviews wounded soldiers and discovers several of the missing forty-one died of shame rather than wounds — suicides recorded as accidents. His certainty cracks. Beat: the hunter beginning to doubt what justice requires.

chapters.title: The Night Nurse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Night nurse Odile Ferrant's POV. Odile, who has covered for Vesper for years without being asked, offers to trade shifts so Vesper can move freely at night — then asks nothing in return, which frightens Vesper more than blackmail would. Beat: grace that cannot be repaid.

chapters.title: Snow on the Wire
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A telegram arrives: Elias is to be deported on a prison transport after the ice closes the harbor — after the Meridian sails. The promise now has an expiration date measured in tides. Beat: panic converted into planning.

chapters.title: What Matron Knew
chapters.summary: Matron Calloway's POV. Renwick confronts Calloway with evidence of falsified duty rosters; she neither confirms nor denies, but afterward she leaves her own copy of the hospital key where Vesper will find it. Beat: silent permission, terrifying and total.

chapters.title: Fitting a Dead Man's Coat
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper alters Harrow's uniform by lamplight, practicing his signature until the transit papers look lived-in, and confronts the question of who they become when they wear another's name. Beat: identity as costume, costume as truth.

chapters.title: The Audit
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper and Renwick POVs. Renwick audits the ward while Vesper answers questions with the precision of seven years' practice; a missing page nearly betrays them until Odile covers the gap. Beat: a duel fought entirely in polite sentences.

chapters.title: Elias Speaks
chapters.summary: Elias Thorne's POV, first time. In the customs house cell, Elias recounts how he ended up classified as enemy despite seven years of service, and why he never blamed Vesper for the silence. Beat: forgiveness offered before it is asked for.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The plan is set: uniform, papers, a forged escort order, Odile at the ward, Calloway looking elsewhere. But Renwick requests Vesper personally accompany him to the customs house at dawn. Beat: the plan and the threat converging on the same hour.

chapters.title: Two Doors, One Corridor
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the customs house, Vesper signs Renwick's statement with one hand while slipping the forged release order across the desk with the other; Elias walks out past them both wearing Harrow's coat. Beat: climax held in a single held breath.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On the quay, the Meridian takes on passengers through freezing fog; Elias hesitates at the gangway, and Vesper tells him the promise was made in peacetime and will be kept in any weather. He sails. Beat: grief and triumph indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Surrender of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Rather than let Renwick find it, Vesper hands him the ledger voluntarily — all forty-one names, plus the story of each omission. Renwick reads in silence, then closes it. Beat: the cost of visibility paid willingly.

chapters.title: What Renwick Wrote
chapters.summary: Renwick's POV. Renwick files his report: the discrepancies attributed to clerical chaos, no informant named, no nurse accused. He keeps one page — Elias's name — as private penance. Beat: justice performed outside the law, by the law's own servant.

chapters.title: Spring, When the Bridge Opens
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Months later, the bridge reopens; Vesper, no longer invisible, begins teaching the town's children to read using the ledger's names, and receives a letter postmarked from across the water containing only the words: tide came in. Beat: inheritance reclaimed — not money, but memory.
